extraction.segment_function: evaluation of alternative interpretations of Arendt regarding technology, mediation, and adaptation

claims.claim: The cumulative effect of mundane adaptations might intensify human isolation or alienation from the earth in its givenness, cutting people off from awareness of their earthbound limitations.
claims.supporting_excerpt:
Another possibility is that, even if these adaptations are small-scale and
mundane, their cumulative effect might be to intensify the isolation or alien-
ation of human beings from the earth in its givenness, cutting people off from
a vital source of awareness of their own earthbound limitations, which is nec-
essary to keep the activity of world building from running amok.

claims.claim: Modern science interposes humanly made technologies of observation and measurement between us and the world, cutting humans off from reality.
claims.supporting_excerpt:
insofar as modern science interposes
humanly made technologies of observation and measurement between us
and the world, it cuts human beings off from the “reality” to which it prom-
ised reliable access.

unresolved_context: Discussion of footnote references to Benjamin Lazier and Waseem Yaqoob, and Arendt's citation of Heisenberg in The Human Condition.
must_not_be_lost: The risk of reading all three types of adaptation solely through the problem of mediation and immediacy.
